properties.name: Benha Nile bridge
properties.note: Second Nile crossing on the Alexandria-Cairo line at Benha.

properties.note: Baghdad Railway crossing of the Euphrates at Jarabulus / Karkamış. Confirmed on OSM ("Karkamış Köprüsü / جسر جرابلس", railway=disused).

properties.note: Abandoned Jezreel Valley / Hejaz railway bridge over the Jordan near Gesher / Naharayim. Confirmed on OSM (railway=abandoned, bridge=yes).

properties.name: Kafr el-Zayyat Nile bridge
properties.note: Nile crossing on the Rosetta branch.

properties.name: Suez Canal railway swing bridge (Kantara / El Ferdan)
properties.note: Railway swing bridge across the Suez Canal linking the Egyptian west-bank line to the Sinai/Palestine railway — the physical Egypt-Levant rail connection.

properties.name: Haifa East / Qishon railway workshops
properties.note: Palestine Railways' main workshops by the Qishon river, adjacent to Haifa East station. Coordinate approximate (Qishon works area).

properties.name: Kadem (Qadam) works & depot
properties.note: Hejaz Railway workshops & depot S of Damascus. Anchored at Kadem station; exact works footprint approximate.

properties.name: Ma'an station workshops
properties.note: Hejaz Railway workshops at Ma'an — a major operating base (and a focal point of the Arab Revolt). Anchored at Ma'an station.

properties.name: Rayak works & depot
properties.note: DHP locomotive workshops, foundry & repair shops — the operational heart of the Beirut–Damascus/Beqaa network and a railway company-town. Site of the junction between the 1,050 mm Beirut–Damascus line and the standard-gauge Rayak–Baalbek–Aleppo line (which moved the transfer point from Damascus to Rayak; Baalbek 1902, Aleppo 1906). The ~133,430 m² factory (≈48 buildings) converted steam engines coal→diesel and served as a technical school; used as a military base in WWII (five "Rayak"-series warplanes assembled at the adjacent airbase). >30 locomotives and ~200 coaches/wagons reportedly still rust on the ~170,000 m² site; the Train/Train NGO proposes a Rayak Railway Museum. Located ~1.1 km NW of the passenger station, on the northern throat that ran under the Baalbek-road bridge toward Homs/Beirut. Site satellite-identified; layout per the DHP factory plan (Rizk 2022).

properties.name: Batn el-Ghoul escarpment descent
properties.note: The Hejaz Railway's dramatic curved descent of the Batn al-Ghul escarpment S of Ma'an. Coordinate = Jabal Batn al-Ghul (approximate); exact rail alignment to verify.

properties.name: Battir railway section
properties.note: The Jaffa–Jerusalem line through the UNESCO World Heritage terraces at Battir, running along the Green Line — a railway / heritage / border collision in a ~2 km stretch. Linear feature anchored at Battir station.

properties.name: Beirut–Damascus rack (Abt) section
properties.note: The 1,050 mm DHP line's Abt rack sections climbing the Lebanon range to the Dahr el-Baidar pass (~1,500 m; gradients reported ~7%) — the region's premier railway engineering feat (opened 1895). Linear feature anchored at the Dahr el-Baidar summit.

properties.name: Ayran tunnel (Amanus / Nur Mountains)
properties.note: Tunnel through the Amanus (Nur) Mountains between Ayran and Fevzipaşa.

properties.name: Bal'a Tunnel (al-Kharq) — Ottoman railway tunnel
properties.note: The only railway tunnel in the West Bank, ~212 m long. Cut through Mount Rasheen ~9 km E of Tulkarm, just E of Bal'a, on the Mas'udiya–Anabta segment of the Eastern/Hejaz branch (our eastern-railway; mapped in OSM as "Old Afula-Nablus Railway"). Local name النفق العثماني / al-Kharq ("the breach"). PORTALS (OSM way 414427473, railway=abandoned tunnel=yes; corridor confirmed on Airbus/Maxar satellite): south 32.323397, 35.147829 · north 32.325232, 35.148359; stored point = midpoint. LENGTH SETTLED: ~212 m measured along the OSM alignment — the 350 m (video) and ~800 m (folklore) figures are overstated; the ~145–240 m estimates were right. DATE contested (Abdul Hamid II-era survey vs 1915 wartime completion under H.A. Meissner). Wikidata Q12409257. Corridor + both portals survive today. [025 correction: on the Afula-Nablus MAIN LINE (Sileh->Mas'udiya, eastern-railway seq4) via El Attara / Kh. Rashin — confirmed as "Tunnel" at Kh. Rashin on Survey of Palestine sheet 16-19 (Anabta, 1942), matching OSM way 414427473 — NOT the Mas'udiya->Anebta arm as 023/024 stated. Precise seq4 corridor geometry pending georeferencing.]

properties.name: Chekka headland tunnel
properties.note: ~1-mile (4,800 ft) tunnel through the Chekka headland on the Lebanese coast.

properties.name: Ras al-Naqoura (Rosh HaNikra) headland tunnels
properties.note: WWII Haifa–Beirut–Tripoli line tunnels bored through the Naqoura headland at the Israel–Lebanon border. Confirmed on OSM ("Rosh HaNikra Railroad", railway=abandoned, tunnel=yes).

properties.name: Taurus (Toros) Mountains tunnels
properties.note: Series of tunnels carrying the line through the Taurus Mountains near Pozantı.

properties.name: Yarmuk gorge tunnels & bridges (Samakh–Deraa)
properties.note: The Samakh–Deraa climb up the Yarmuk gorge: 8 tunnels (~1,100 m) and 329 bridges/aqueducts over 73 km (+529 m). Relocated onto the route 2026-07-26 (was ~2 km S). Verified features (Tim, imagery): tunnel W portal 32.725541,35.722512 / E portal 32.727303,35.727710; bridge 32.732655,35.736110; Yarmouk river crossing 32.712460,35.698890. Much of the mid-gorge alignment is at the Al-Wahda (ex-Maqarin) dam site, built 2004–05.
